title: Default run stays review-only even when ux lane is added; fix:true still unexercised
detail: Orchestrator runs stay review-only (review.fix.mode='review-only'). The 2026-06-18T15:22 run added the ux lane (lanes:[review,schema,ux]) for the first time but the REVIEW lane still kept fix:false — note ux auto-applies its own 3 fixes via its own dryRun:false path, independent of review fix.mode. The medium-effort review fix path remains unverified in this history.

title: openIssues trend is wildly non-monotone: 11->14->12->1->0->21->172->174->22 across runs
detail: openIssues went 11,14,12,1,0,21,172,174,22. The 0->21->172->174 escalation after the 06-16 clean run confirmed the baseline was fragile and code churn refills the queue aggressively. The 22 on 2026-06-19T21:01 is the FIRST post-uxAuto-fix pure code-only figure (review 22 + schema 0 + drift 0, ux excluded) — back to a sane review-only magnitude after the 165-issue UX flood was gated out. Confirms the openIssues formula change (lever-openissues-code-only) produces a code-health scalar that is both smaller and more interpretable than the ux-contaminated 174. NOTE: 174 was dominated by ux totalIssues (165), not review newFindings; now that ux is gated behind uxAuto, openIssues is again a pure review+schema signal. Treat a 0 as 'queue drained', never 'nothing to find'.

title: schema runtime lane reports ~5 findings on dirty runs, null once, now THREE consecutive fully-clean 0s
detail: Runtime lane reported ~5 findings on non-clean runs (first run had 8 + 2 errors). On 2026-06-18T13:32 it returned null; on 2026-06-18T15:22, 2026-06-19T18:35, AND 2026-06-19T21:01 it returned runtimeFindings=0, runtimeErrors=0, driftRemaining=0 — THREE consecutive fully-clean schema lane results. The runtime lane (buildCliArgs->run.py boundary) is productive on churn but goes quiet when the tree is clean; a 0 is now firmly interpretable as clean (distinct from the null failure mode). Check schemaHistory path when schema=null.

title: runtimeErrors only appeared in the first run (2); zero across all 9 runs since
detail: First run had 2 runtimeErrors + 8 runtimeFindings; all subsequent runs (now 9 total) have 0 errors, including the latest fully-clean 0-finding run. Either the boundary stabilized or earlier runs' findings were resolved out-of-band. Don't assume errors are gone — re-run objective:runtime after any CLI change.

title: coverageDelta is NaN on every run — coverage lane never runs under objective:runtime
detail: All runs set objective:runtime (default), so coverageDelta reports 'NaN' every time (now 8 runs confirmed). To get a real coverage trend you must pass objective:coverage|both|all; the default lane produces no coverage signal.

title: driftRemaining is 0 on all runs — GUI<->run.py flags stay aligned
detail: driftRemaining=0 across all runs (now 8 with signal). Either drift is genuinely clean or check:schema was already applied earlier. Drift lane is currently a low-value no-op; budget agent time on the runtime lane instead.

title: Verified review findings severity is run-dependent; medium dominates high-volume runs, low/medium split on low-volume
detail: Severity distribution varies per run. 2026-06-18T13:32: high=5, medium=12, low=4. 2026-06-18T15:22: high=6, medium=13, low=2. 2026-06-19T18:35: high=2, medium=3, low=4 (lowest total=9, low-dominant). 2026-06-19T21:01: high=3, medium=15, low=4 (total=22, MEDIUM-dominant again). Pattern sharpens: medium is the modal bucket whenever total findings are high (>=12); low edges medium only at the very lowest volumes (9). high stays in a narrow 2-6 band regardless of volume. Set fix:true if you want the long tail (medium is where the bulk lives); high/critical alone rarely justify a fix run.

title: review-only runs report findings but don't fix them; openIssues only drops via external action
detail: Every run has review.fix.mode='review-only' (fix:false). The 11->1->0 openIssues drop between 06-15 and 06-16 happened WITHOUT any review fix:true run — the backlog was cleared outside the orchestrator. The 0->21->172->174 escalation confirmed the queue refills as code changes (and the ux lane added a large population). A clean review-only run is not evidence the code is clean, only that nothing new was flagged.

title: delta_from_last is null on every run — inter-run delta tracking is not wired
detail: signals.delta_from_last is null in all runs, so you cannot read 'better/worse than last run' from the envelope. Compute deltas yourself from openIssues/verified/runtimeFindings across history files.

title: Orchestrator completes with empty phases_failed on every run
detail: status='complete' and phases_failed=[] on all runs, even ones that surfaced runtimeErrors, 174 openIssues, or a null schema lane. Don't treat 'complete' as 'no problems' — phase success only means the lane ran, not that the code is healthy. Read result.review/schema/ux for actual signal.

title: dirtyTree=false on all runs — the dirty-tree fix downgrade is unverified
detail: dirtyTree was false in all runs (all review-only), so the 'fix:true gets downgraded to review-only on a dirty git tree' guard has never actually fired here. Don't rely on history to confirm that guard works; test it deliberately before trusting it.

title: verified == newFindings on every run — no carryover/recheck of prior issues
detail: In all runs result.review.verified equals result.review.newFindings (each run only reports freshly-detected issues, never re-checks the prior backlog). 2026-06-19T21:01 confirms again: verified=22, newFindings=22. openIssues is a count of NEW findings (plus ux totalIssues when ux lane is on), not a persistent tracker — so a downward trend means fewer new bugs, not that old ones were fixed by this workflow.

title: schema lane can silently return null — but also returns full data when healthy (intermittent)
detail: On 2026-06-18T13:32 the schema result field was null despite schema being in lanes. The 2026-06-18T15:22, 2026-06-19T18:35, and 2026-06-19T21:01 runs show the lane CAN return full data (runtimeFindings=0, driftRemaining=0) — so null is a genuine intermittent failure mode, not a constant. The schemaHistory path (gui-movie-director-schema-self-improve/iterations.jsonl) is the authoritative log; null result may mean internal error. Always check schemaHistory when schema=null.

title: No stable baseline: clean runs are immediately re-broken by code churn
detail: The 2026-06-16 clean run (openIssues=0) was broken within hours — 21 findings on 06-18T13:32, then 172 on 06-18T15:22, then 174 on 06-19T18:35, then 22 (pure code-only) on 06-19T21:01. No clean baseline has survived to the next run. Re-establishing a baseline requires a fix:true run to clear the queue AND a code-churn freeze; review-only runs cannot produce a durable baseline.

title: SUPERSEDED: the 21-finding spike was dwarfed by a 172-finding run hours later
detail: Recorded the 2026-06-18T13:32 21-finding spike as the largest single-run count. SUPERSEDED by openissues-172-spike-three-lane which shows the same code-churn driver producing 172 findings (8x larger) just hours later, and the non-monotone pattern (openissues-converges-to-zero) is the durable insight. This specific spike magnitude is no longer the high-water mark.

title: 174 openIssues high-water mark was a 3-lane ux-contaminated run; post-uxAuto-fix pure-code runs sit ~22
detail: The 2026-06-19T18:35 run produced 174 openIssues = review.newFindings(9) + ux.totalIssues(165), ~95% ux-sourced. That was the high-water mark UNDER the old openIssues formula (review+schema+drift+ux). After the uxAuto gate fix (2026-06-19T18:51), the 2026-06-19T21:01 pure review+schema run produced openIssues=22 (review 22 + schema 0 + drift 0, ux excluded) — confirming the new code-only scalar sits an order of magnitude below the ux-contaminated 174. When ux lane is enabled, openIssues is NOT comparable to review-only figures — always split result.ux.totalIssues from result.review.newFindings before trending.

title: ux totalIssues (165) dwarfs review newFindings (9) — openIssues stops being a review-only metric
detail: Second ux-lane run: ux.totalIssues=165 vs review.newFindings=9; merged openIssues=174 was ~95% ux-sourced (up from 88% on the first ux run, because review findings shrank 21->9 while ux held ~150-165). Treating openIssues as a code-review regression signal is invalid once ux lane is enabled — ux surveys every view's UX issues (field clarity, loading states, empty states), a different and much larger population than code bugs. Always read result.ux.totalIssues separately from result.review.newFindings; never trend them together as one number.

title: ux auto-fix lifts avg score ~0.5 points per run fixing only 3 of ~150 issues
detail: The 2026-06-18T15:22 ux lane surveyed 23 views (avg 4.82/10) and auto-fixed 3 issues, raising the average to 5.36/10 (+0.54). The 2026-06-19T18:35 run surveyed 23 views (avg 3.91/10) and auto-fixed 3 issues, raising to 4.43/10 (+0.52). The ux fix path is functional and applies fixes via its own dryRun:false control — independent of review.fix.mode (which stayed review-only). The +0.5/3-fix lever ratio is consistent across two runs. Note: avg DROPPED 5.36->3.91 between runs (different view mix / churn re-introduced regressions), so absolute score is not yet monotone — but the per-run fix delta is stable. Confirms ux lane is a real lever, unlike the review lane's unverified fix path.

title: UX avg score baseline hovers ~4-5/10 across 23 views; absolute score is non-monotone run-to-run
detail: Two ux-lane baselines now: 2026-06-18T15:22 avgScoreBefore=4.82, 2026-06-19T18:35 avgScoreBefore=3.91 (DOWN 0.91 despite a +0.52 fix delta the prior run). The before-score dropped because code churn re-introduced UX regressions between runs. Even after fixing 3 each time, avg only reaches ~4.4-5.4/10. The UX surface has significant debt (field clarity, loading states, empty states) that the review/schema lanes cannot surface, AND fixes do not durably stick — the same views re-regress. The ux lane is the only lane that sees this surface; it is additive signal, but a single fix run is not durable without a code-churn freeze.

title: schema lane returned a fully-clean result (0 findings, 0 errors, 0 drift) — now three consecutive clean runs
detail: 2026-06-18T15:22 was the first schema lane result with runtimeFindings=0, runtimeErrors=0, AND driftRemaining=0 simultaneously; 2026-06-19T18:35 and 2026-06-19T21:01 repeat it. Prior clean-ish runs still had a few runtime findings or a null result. Three consecutive clean runs suggest the schema->CLI boundary (buildCliArgs->run.py) is currently healthy — the GUI schemas and run.py flags are aligned. Re-confirm after any CLI/schema edit; a 0 is now interpretable as genuinely clean (distinct from the null failure mode).

title: Command views render a blank/black main panel with no form on first navigation
detail: The dominant UX defect class: several views (t2i, video-quality, video-generate, faceswap, model-check, jobs) render an empty black void on first load because CommandForm only mounts AFTER useDefaultState resolves server defaults, and the canvas is bare in the meantime. There is no header, breadcrumb, empty-state, or loading skeleton — the user cannot tell a loading failure from an empty state from a broken render. Affects every createCommandView() view until guarded. The VLM caption reads these as 'a large, empty black panel' / 'no primary action button visible'.

title: Guard CommandViewShell with an actionable empty-state instead of a dead black panel
detail: Adopted fix for blank-panel views: when a view yields no form children (silent render failure), CommandViewShell now renders an actionable 'This view has nothing to show' message plus a .empty-view-state CSS class, so the canvas is never a bare void. Applied to video-quality-01 (score held 2->2 but the panel is no longer dead). Generalizes to every createCommandView view — always provide a non-blocking empty/loading placeholder while useDefaultState resolves or when children fail to mount.

title: Wrap command views in a persistent title header (reuse ModelCheckView inline-style convention)
detail: Adopted fix for blank/unlabeled panels: wrap the generated view (e.g. T2lView) in a container that renders a persistent h2 title plus a dim description line, matching the existing ModelCheckView inline-style convention and reusing --text-bright/--text-dim CSS variables. Result: the main panel is never blank/unlabeled and the user can always tell which view is active. Applied to t2i-01 (score 3->9). This is the higher-impact sibling of the empty-state guard — it also labels healthy renders.

title: Sidebar active-state logic is correct; the CSS is too faint for the VLM (and users) to read as selected
detail: Layout.tsx already computes an `active` class on the sidebar item when currentView.action===cmd.id, so the routing logic is NOT the bug. The defect is that .sidebar-item.active (global.css:91) uses only a faint background + accent left border + accent text that reads as indistinguishable from inactive. Strengthen with an --accent color-mix tinted background + font-weight 600 (adopted in video-quality-02, score 2->8) so the selected item is unmistakable. Do NOT re-investigate the Layout logic when the active cue looks missing.

title: toSections silently discards any schema field without a `section` property
detail: Latent trap: schemas/toForm.ts toSections does `if (!f.section) continue;`, so any field lacking a `section` is silently dropped from the rendered form with NO error. Confirmed instance: faceswap schema's 'LoRA Path' field {key:'lora'} has no section, so the documented LoRA control never appears in the UI and users cannot set a custom face-swap LoRA despite the schema declaring it. Either assign every schema field a section, or make toSections fall back to a default 'Advanced' section instead of dropping sectionless fields.

title: ViewDescriptor id MUST equal the useCommandJob/SCHEMA_MAP action key
detail: Latent routing/state bug: VideoGenerateView registers with descriptor id 'vid-generate', but every other reference uses 'video-generate' (useCommandJob('video-generate'), action='video-generate', SCHEMA_MAP['video-generate']). If routing or useDefaultState keys off the descriptor id, the schema-defaults fetch and action routing resolve against different keys — contributing to blank render and breaking per-view state persistence. Convention: keep the descriptor id identical to the schema action key AND the CLI action, as the sibling video views (VideoRelay etc.) already do.

title: Disabled submit buttons give no reason — no inline hint listing missing required inputs
detail: Recurring UX gap: schema.isDisabled(state) returns true when required inputs are unset (e.g. faceswap input_image/face), greying out the primary action, but nothing in the UI explains WHY or what the user must do. No required-field callout, no helper text, no 'Upload X and Y to enable Z'. A first-time user staring at a disabled button has no path forward. When schema.isDisabled(state) is true, render an InlineError or small hint near the btn-row listing the missing required inputs.

title: Sidebar nav items are non-semantic divs — not keyboard-focusable, no aria-current
detail: Accessibility defect: all navigation entries (Gallery, Config, Jobs, every command) are plain <div> elements with onClick handlers (Layout.tsx). No role='button', no tabIndex, no aria-current — invisible to Tab-key navigation and screen readers cannot announce them. The sidebar <aside> is also not a <nav aria-label>. Fix: render nav items as <button> (or role='button' tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown Enter/Space), wrap in <nav aria-label='Views'>, set aria-current='page' on the active item. A keyboard-only or assistive-tech user cannot reach any view currently.

title: Avg UX score ~4-5/10; ~3 fixes per run, ~17 high-severity issues remain — needs ~8 iters to reach ~7.0
detail: Measured baseline from the 23-view scan: avg UX score 4.82 (first run) / 3.91 (second run), ~150-165 issues total (~20 high). With maxIters:3 and dryRun:false, only 3 fixes applied per run (score ceiling ~4.4-5.4/10), leaving ~17 high-severity issues unfixed. The blank-panel/active-nav/header fixes each move a single view 3-7 points, so the lever-per-iter ratio is high but the volume of low-scoring views (t2i=3, video-quality=2, video-generate=3, faceswap=3, image-restore=4, model-check=4) exceeds a 3-iter budget. Suggested next run: maxIters:8, dryRun:false -> expect avg ~7.0. image-pipeline scored null/0 issues (healthy / not reached) and can be skipped to save budget.

title: VLM caption can misread a correctly-wired feature as missing when the visual cue is too subtle
detail: Recurring false-positive class: the VLM (and by extension users) reports 'No active/selected highlight' and 'no primary action button visible' even when the underlying TS logic is correct. video-quality-02 and t2i-02 both reported a missing active-nav cue, but Layout.tsx already applies the `active` class — the CSS was just too faint. Treat 'feature is missing' captions as visual-prominence problems first (strengthen the CSS) before investigating the logic. Distinguish 'logic absent' from 'logic present but invisible' by reading the source, not by trusting the caption.

title: Absolute-path-as-info-disclosure is a FALSE POSITIVE when the path is functional identity
detail: Review lane flags api/models.ts handleListLoras/handleListVaes returning absolute filesystem paths to the client as 'info disclosure'. But lora.path is LOAD-BEARING: LoraField.tsx uses it as the <option value>, copy-to-clipboard (for CLI reuse), and the selected value flows to run.py --lora. Stripping to basename BREAKS the selector + copy feature. Verified 2026-06-19: grep frontend shows lora.path used as identity key at LoraField.tsx:165/199/204. Suppress this finding class; the threat model is weak anyway (unauthenticated localhost dev tool).

title: getReader()-throws finding misses the null-stream guard 67 lines above
detail: Review flagged lib/subprocess.ts:210 'getReader() throws outside try/catch, leaves job stuck running'. But a guard at lines 143-152 checks `if (!proc.stdout || !proc.stderr)` and finalizes-as-failed BEFORE the getReader calls are reached. The review lane pattern-matched the call site without scanning upward for an existing guard. Verified 2026-06-19: guard present, finding is dead. Generalizes: review lacks duplicate/guard awareness — always scan surrounding context before applying an error-handling finding.

title: UX auto-detect made the 'cheap routine scan' cost 77 agents/2.6M tok — now gated behind uxAuto:true (gate CONFIRMED working)
detail: A BARE invocation auto-detected the GUI server (Resolve phase) and appended the UX lane, surveying all 23 views. In review-only/dryRun the UX lane fixes 0 issues, so this cost ~50 agents + VLM calls for no actionable output — turning the documented 'cheap review+schema scan' into a 77-agent/2.6M-token/55min run. FIXED 2026-06-19: auto-detect now requires uxAuto:true (default off). Opt in via uxAuto:true or lanes:['ux']/'all'. CONFIRMED 2026-06-19T21:01: a bare two-lane run (lanes:[review,schema]) returned ux=null and did NOT spawn the UX lane — the gate holds, and openIssues returned to a pure code-only 22 (no 165-issue UX flood).

title: openIssues now excludes UX noise — code-health debt only (review+schema+drift); CONFIRMED at 22
detail: Resolves the openissues-converges-to-zero metric: openIssues was review+schema+drift+ux, so the 174 high-water mark was ~95% unfixed UX (165/174). In review-only the UX lane fixes 0, so the scalar + its run-over-run trend reflected screenshot variance, not code health. FIXED 2026-06-19: openIssues = review verified + schema runtimeErrors + remaining drift. UX tracked separately as uxOpenIssues + avgUxScore. Delta agent recomputes prev from components so the trend stays comparable across the formula change. CONFIRMED 2026-06-19T21:01: first post-fix pure-code run produced openIssues=22 (review.verified 22 + schema.runtimeErrors 0 + driftRemaining 0), an order of magnitude below the ux-contaminated 174 and a plausible code-health magnitude.

title: Verify a finding's usage + surrounding guards BEFORE applying — effort:low FP rate ~50%
detail: On the 2026-06-19 run, 4 of 8 'verified' review findings were false-positive or already-fixed: (1) lora/vae path 'info disclosure' — path is functional identity; (2) subprocess getReader 'throws' — guarded 67 lines above; (3) model-check/config stderr 'leak' — localhost dev tool, forwarding aids debugging. Adversarial verify reported upheld=0 yet 8 stayed 'verified' — it does NOT filter context-free pattern matches. CHECK before applying: grep frontend usage of the flagged symbol AND scan ~70 lines around the site for an existing guard.

title: Review finding volume scales with changed-file surface; 22 here vs 9 prior — medium-dominant tail grows first
detail: 2026-06-19T21:01 surfaced 22 review findings (verified=22) vs 9 on 2026-06-19T18:35. Severity split: high=3, medium=15, low=4. The volume jump (9->22) tracks a wider changed-file surface this run, and the growth landed almost entirely in the MEDIUM bucket (3->15, +12) while high held near-flat (2->3) and low held (4->4). Implication for fix-targeting: when scope widens, expect the medium tail to balloon — a fix:true run is justified once medium crosses ~12-15 because that is where the bulk of actionable (non-false-positive) debt accumulates; high rarely moves enough to trigger on its own. Pair with pattern-verify-usage-before-applying since the medium tail also carries the false-positive load.

title: W3 deep fix (deferred 2026-06-20): make review-optimize info-disclosure/error-handling/security dimensions usage-aware to cut FP at source
detail: Root cause of the ~50% effort:low false-positive rate: the adversarial-verify gate reports upheld=0 yet findings stay verified (2026-06-19T21:01: 22 verifiedFindings, 0 upheld, 14 in security). The gate does not filter context-free pattern matches. Fix at the SOURCE by editing .claude/workflows/gui-movie-director-review-optimize.js: in the info-disclosure / error-handling / security dimension prompts, REQUIRE the reviewer to (a) grep call-site usage of the flagged symbol/endpoint and (b) scan ~70 lines around the site plus the auth middleware for an existing guard or benign context BEFORE flagging; downgrade severity or drop when a guard/benign context exists. This moves the usage-check from fix-time (pattern-verify-usage-before-applying) to flag-time. Implementation is a code edit to the child workflow, not a run-time arg.

title: Do NOT bulk-apply the effort:low security/info-disclosure cluster via effort:medium+fix:true - adversarial gate is broken (upheld=0)
detail: 2026-06-19T21:01 reported 22 verifiedFindings with adversarialUpheld=0 and its nextStep suggested effort:medium+fix:true. Ignore that for the security-dim cluster (api/models.ts listLoras/listVaes abs paths; api/config.ts handleVerifyPython stderr + validatePythonPath substring; api/model-check.ts stderr). review-optimize.knowledge.jsonl already documents several as recurring patterns (verify-python-leaks-stderr, model-check-leaks-stderr, validate-python-path-substring-not-prefix) and unfixed-recurrence-is-real-not-noise notes recurring findings have FP-rate 0 - so they may be real, but the broken gate (upheld=0) makes verification unreliable EITHER way. Manually triage before any fix run; treat this cluster as UNVERIFIED, not confirmed-FP and not confirmed-real.

title: 2 HIGH-severity candidates from 2026-06-19T21:01 awaiting manual triage (read legitimate, bypassed broken gate)
detail: (1) frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts:80 - job_failed handler never restores partial outputFiles from the WS message (correctness, high). (2) lib/knowledge-extractor.ts:361 - callDeepSeek fetch has no AbortSignal timeout; can hang the single-threaded Bun event loop indefinitely (error-handling, high). Both showed adversarialUpheld=0 like everything else (broken gate) but read as real bugs on inspection. Verify + fix manually; do not wait for the review lane verify to confirm, and do not let avoid-bulk-autofix-loweffort-security-cluster block these two - they are the highest-signal subset.
